name: T13-am-kill
description: Background, then kill the process 5s later.

steps.why: settle and let one foreground disk flush land (~5s, stats.first_upload_flush_interval_ms) so the FG/BG split has a positive control. This used to be 35s to clear the 30s stats.minimum_upload_interval_ms floor, but that floor is armed ONLY by a flush-path upload (stats.rs: last_flush_upload_time), and shared-core 184c3229 removed the workflow trigger that used to fire one at launch. A fresh process now reaches ON_STOP unarmed, so the long wait gated nothing. Verified: ON_STOP upload allowed 1.88s after a periodic upload.

kill lands at ~ON_STOP+390ms, reliably BEFORE the ack. Bracketed on a Pixel 10: +390ms and +865ms both beat the ack, while +1.32s lost to a 974ms ack. Ack latency ranges 633-1535ms, so no wait reliably lands on the ack's side -- aim at the side that reliably tests something. This exercises the recovery path: the disk write survives (+25ms) and the snapshot is re-uploaded on next launch, verified by uuid.
long enough to see whether the snapshot is recovered on the next process start
